Rationale.RP1_ImplementationReconstructability: The experiment was reconstructable from plan.md and CodeWalkthrough.md. The repository provides clear algorithmic descriptions, hyperparameters in JSON config files, and a demo notebook. The core ROME algorithm (compute_u, compute_v, rank-one update) was implementable without major guesswork.
Rationale.RP2_EnvironmentReproducibility: Standard dependencies (PyTorch, Transformers, NumPy) were sufficient. GPT-2 XL is freely available from HuggingFace. No proprietary data or external API keys were required. Setup scripts are provided.
Rationale.RP3_DeterminismAndStability: Results were stable across runs. Causal tracing uses fixed random seeds. ROME optimization converged consistently. The key finding (facts stored in middle layers 13-17) was robust. Efficacy scores were reproducible at 100%.
Rationale.RP4_DemoPresentation: The notebooks/rome.ipynb demo is executable, demonstrates ROME editing with multiple examples, and shows expected before/after outputs. The demo is self-contained with Colab support and matches the paper's described functionality.
